title_ar: Analytics: الداتا البايظة والإحصاء والـsemantic model والتقرير (2/3)
title_en: Analytics: dirty data and applied steps, statistics from mean to A/B, the semantic model and the report (part 2 of 3)
how_to_read: sentences[].w = first..last word id inside this chapter; word k (0-based) of the sentence is first+k and `ar` is the spoken text (its space-separated tokens are those words); fr = [start_frame, end_frame] at 24 fps from the word map; impact = hook words (id=text); num = spoken numbers with data-contract fact ids; first_mention = glossary terms to chip (id=term); dup = same claim in another chapter. Anchor with {word, lead_frames} only. Visual candidates are ideas, never footage.

constraints.anchors: {word, lead_frames} only; never seconds or frames; event frame = word start - lead_frames
constraints.lead_frames: kinetic word -3, graphic state change -2, shot cut -4..-6 (inside a pause >= 200 ms), counter starts at the number word
constraints.density: >= 20 events/min; no gap > 4 s without an event (hold <= 6 s with reason); shot median 6-12 s, max 25 s (shots > 12 s: an event every 3 s)
constraints.coverage: every sentence >= 1 anchored event; >= 80 % of sentences a mechanism event; every spoken number and every first-mention term on screen
constraints.kinetic: 8-20 kinetic words per minute; <= 6 words and <= 2 lines on screen; impact word 1-2 words
constraints.fx: hero (real-time 3D) <= 5 % of chapter frames (ADR-002 RT5); fx_tier lite|standard|hero
constraints.text: text on busy backgrounds needs a plate or halo; sizes and safe areas: 04 sections 3.2 and 3.4
banned: invented numbers (every number: data-contract id or source sentence)
constraints.components: use only frozen components (harness/schemas/components/); requests go to corpus/specs/_component_requests.jsonl
constraints.chapter_rhythm: problem -> mental model -> progressive visual -> worked example -> prediction -> failure (crit) -> fix (ok) -> callback -> artifact (per chapter, not per sentence)

storyboard_notes.text: Micro-dive (1.7 min): use the consistent 'side note' card treatment (same card grammar every time).
Restating dive: treat it as a visual callback that reuses the trunk chapter's assets (see `restates` in continuity); the fact-checker checks its numbers against the trunk.

sentences.ar: طيب نروح للقسم الثالث الإحصاء المتوسط الوسيط والعينات
sentences.en: Okay, let's go to the third section: statistics, mean, median and samples.

sentences.ar: دلوقتي الداتا نضفت إزاي بقى نوصفها صح من غير ما نضحك على نفسنا
sentences.en: Now that the data is clean, how do we describe it properly without fooling ourselves?

sentences.ar: بصوا على المشهد اللي قدامنا ده الفكرة بتشرح نفسها حرفيا
sentences.en: Look at the scene in front of us; the idea explains itself, literally.

sentences.ar: تخيلوا سلة مشتريات قيمتها تسحبت فجأة من 90 يورو ل600 يورو
sentences.en: Imagine a shopping basket whose value was suddenly pulled from 90 euros to 600 euros.

sentences.ar: على الشمال هنلاقي الـmean أو المتوسط بيجري وراها بسرعة وبيزيد معاه
sentences.en: On the left, the mean, or average, runs after it quickly and rises with it.

sentences.ar: بس على اليمين الـmedian أو الوسيط وقف مكانه ثابت ما تحركش
sentences.en: But on the right, the median stopped in place, stable, and did not move.

sentences.ar: ده بيثبت إنك تعتمد على رقم واحد بس دي فكرة خطيرة
sentences.en: This proves that relying on a single number is a dangerous idea.

sentences.ar: لأن طفرة واحدة تقدر تشد المتوسط كله معاه وتبوّظلك التحليل
sentences.en: Because one spike can drag the whole average along with it and wreck your analysis.

sentences.ar: وده بياخدنا لحقيقة مهمة جداً في الشغل العملي
sentences.en: And this takes us to a very important truth in practical work.

sentences.ar: احنا دايماً بناخد عينات
sentences.en: We always take samples.

sentences.ar: تخيل مجتمع فيه 5000 طلب
sentences.en: Imagine a population of 5000 orders.

sentences.ar: ومن هنا بندخل على القسم الرابع فترات الثقة واختبارات الـ A -B إزاي نختبر ادعاءاتنا ونكون واثقين بجد
sentences.en: From here we enter the fourth section: confidence intervals and A/B tests, how to test our claims and be truly confident.

sentences.ar: لما بنقول إننا واثقين بنسبة 95 % ده مش معناه إن الرقم جواه بنسبة 95 %
sentences.en: When we say we are 95% confident, that does not mean the number is inside the range with 95% probability.

sentences.ar: زي ما ناس كتير فاهمة الفكرة إن دي ثقة في العملية نفسها
sentences.en: As many people understand it; the idea is that it is confidence in the process itself.

sentences.ar: والخمسة اللي خيبوا هينوروا أحمر بوضوح
sentences.en: And the five that missed will light up red, clearly.

sentences.ar: وعشان نختبر صح بنعمل A -B Tests
sentences.en: And to test properly we do A/B tests.

sentences.ar: لازم نحدد حجم الأثر اللي يستاهل ونخلي قوة الاختبار 80 % ونحسب حجم العينة المطلوب لكل مجموعة
sentences.en: We must set the effect size worth caring about, set the power of the test at 80%, and compute the required sample size per group.

sentences.ar: نيجي بقى للقسم الخامس سياق الفلتر وتقارير الـdashboard
sentences.en: Now to the fifth section: filter context and dashboard reports.

sentences.ar: الأرقام جاهزة إزاي هتظهر في التقارير
sentences.en: The numbers are ready, so how will they show up in the reports?

sentences.ar: الـmeasures اللي بنعملها مش مجرد عواميد ثابتة دي دوال بتتغير حسب الفلتر
sentences.en: The measures we build are not just fixed columns; they are functions that change with the filter.

sentences.ar: الجدول اللي قدامنا بيبين ازاي نفس المعادلة بتطلع 3 قيم مختلفة تحت 3 فلاتر أو slicers مختلفين
sentences.en: The table in front of us shows how the same formula yields 3 different values under 3 different filters or slicers.

facts.rule: A number goes on screen with its fact id as `ref`/`data_refs`. `unmatched_numbers` are spoken but have no data-contract fact: their source is the sentence itself (a valid `s:` ref); never replace them with a different figure.

referenced.ctx: The counted confidence-interval coverage converges on 95 %.

glossary.rule: Explain the term in Egyptian Arabic the first time it appears; then use the original term naturally, in Latin script, inside Arabic sentences.
glossary.register_ar: Natural Egyptian, clear, calm, professional. Use إحنا and خلّينا نشوف and ببساطة where they help. No heavy Modern Standard Arabic. No exaggerated slang. Numbers are spoken naturally in Egyptian but displayed as Western digits.
glossary.register_en: Plain, direct, unhurried. Short sentences. No hype, no "imagine that…", no rhetorical questions that are not real prediction prompts. Say the number, then pause for half a beat before the next sentence — the pause is where the viewer reads the screen.
glossary.never_translate_rule: Explain them in Egyptian Arabic the first time they appear, then use the original term naturally.
glossary.on_screen: Western digits, Latin terms in LTR isolates, Egyptian Arabic copy (no MSA), no per-letter animation (04 section 3.4).

components.does: One whole word (or a tatweel-joined compound like الـKafka) on screen; never split per letter.
Up to 6 kinetic words on at most 2 lines, each word arriving on its own spoken word anchor.
A technical term chip (Latin in an LTR isolate) with an optional Arabic gloss; 28 px floor if spoken.
A counter that rolls from the previous value to the target over the spoken number (preset count).
An arrow from a label to a target layer (or a named part of it, 'layer.part').
Failure beat: glitch + low thud; flashes stay <= 3/s (WCAG 2.3.1).
Fix beat: the target settles into place with a settle chime.
The shot camera: move + ease + intensity; drift always on; optional impact nudges (<= 4 px) on anchors.
Match cut between a layer of this shot and one of the next.
Lower-third caption for a source, term, speaker or location.
Draw an SVG path (stroke reveal; RTL by default for Arabic layouts).
A data table (<= 8 columns, <= 12 visible rows); numbers come from a data_ref.
A fact table with dimension tables in 3D.
A panel of 1-6 KPIs with status colours.
Deep-Dive entry card with parent chapter and prerequisite concepts.
